rows.notes: The study is explicitly a narrative review (title 'Review'; Section 1 describes an exploratory literature search across ScienceDirect, Scopus, Springer, Wiley). It reports no own data, experiment, survey or model runs. Its mention of WA+ (Section 3.1) only describes the framework developed by IWMI/IHE-Delft/FAO, notes its strong focus on satellite remote sensing and that it has been widely used, citing other work [55-57]; it reports no own result on remote sensing bridging data gaps or improving inter-agency coordination. The statement that a key output of water accounting should be a common information base acceptable to all stakeholders (Sections 3.3 and 6) is a normative proposition attributed to [21,22], not a finding.

notes: Study is a literature review with proposed indicator definitions (WP, IE equations) and compiled tables of devices, sensors, models and Kc-VI relations; no primary results of its own. Text appears complete; some pages are duplicated/garbled from PDF extraction but no content loss affecting rating.
